newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC sees fundamentally firmer Swiss franc.
newsitem.headline: SBC sees fundamentally firmer Swiss franc.

text.p: The Swiss franc should strengthen against the mark on the basis of purchasing power parity (PPP), but future Swiss monetary policy and the franc's safe-haven role before EMU will play key roles, Swiss Bank Corp said.

In its monthly financial magazine, SBC said its SBC Brinson bond and currency research group expected the Swiss National Bank to maintain its generous policy this year given the weak domestic economy.
It also gave as its prime scenario eight countries launching the single currency in 1999, which should make the euro solid and prevent investors' flight into the franc.
"In all, one can ascertain that economic fundamentals point in the long term to a stronger franc," it said, adding:

"Should immoderate appreciation tendencies emerge in the Swiss franc in the run-up to European monetary union, one can expect the SNB to countersteer massively, if necessary with an upper limit for the franc exchange rate."
